mods:mods.mods:abstract: Hydrogen was proposed as an alternative fuel in 1968, marking the start of its journey toward becoming a sustainable energy source. Although several methods exist for producing green hydrogen, water electrolysis remains the most promising because it is compatible with renewable energy and can produce high-purity hydrogen without carbon emissions. In this review, we propose a comparative framework linking catalyst durability, operating conditions, and LCOH to technology readiness. Our findings show that improved catalysts, better electrolyzer designs, and tighter integration with renewable energy have all contributed to higher efficiency and greater durability. However, high energy use, material degradation, and challenges in large-scale production are major obstacles to the widespread use of green hydrogen. This highlights the need for focused research to develop sustainable, cost-effective production methods. Overall, this review offers practical guidance for improving catalyst performance and advancing more efficient, durable, and scalable green hydrogen systems for future applications.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: The metallization of polymer substrates is a critical enabling technology for extending the functionality of lightweight polymers and polymer matrix composites in electronics, biomedical devices, aerospace, energy systems, and emerging engineering applications. However, conventional metallization techniques are often limited by thermal sensitivity, poor interfacial adhesion, restricted scalability, and environmental concerns when applied to polymeric materials. These challenges have driven growing interest in cold spray as a low-temperature, solid-state deposition process that can overcome fundamental incompatibility between metals and polymers although preserving substrate integrity. This review critically reports recent progress in cold spray metallization of polymers, with an emphasis on process fundamentals, numerical modeling, materials design, and application-driven developments. Computational approaches (including CFD, smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH), and coupled thermo-mechanical finite element modeling) are reviewed for their role in elucidating particle–polymer interaction mechanisms such as impact-induced deformation, heat generation, interfacial stress evolution, and localized bonding phenomena. Advances in cold spray process variants, surface activation strategies, composite and additive-assisted feedstocks, and integration with additive manufacturing are discussed in the context of expanding the processing window and enabling tailored interface engineering. The review further surveys demonstrated applications in electronics and Electro-Magnetic Interference (EMI) shielding, biomedical coatings, aerospace and energy systems, and emerging sectors requiring scalable, multifunctional polymer–metal systems. Despite significant progress, challenges related to adhesion durability, process reproducibility, scalability, sustainability, and predictive modeling remain inadequately addressed. Addressing these issues will require coordinated advances in experimental characterization, process control, materials design, and multiscale simulation. Overall, cold spray metallization is positioned as a robust and versatile platform for next-generation polymer surface functionalization and hybrid manufacturing.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Accurate prediction of stress and deformation fields in laminated composite plates remains challenging due to the nonlinear nature of the governing physical processes. Traditional numerical methods often provide accurate solutions but at significant computational costs. To address this, this study proposes a two-stage physics-guided generative framework for efficient, high-fidelity response prediction. In the first stage, a Conditional Variational Autoencoder (CVAE) captures the global response patterns conditioned on structural parameters. In the second stage, CVAE outputs are further refined using a Conditional Residual Split Model integrated with a physics-guided regularization strategy to improve accuracy while preserving physically meaningful spatial characteristics. The results demonstrate excellent agreement with finite element solutions, yielding median Structural Similarity Index values of 0.997 and 0.984 for deflection and stress, respectively. Stochastic analysis confirms that the predictions remain stable under identical input conditions despite stochastic latent sampling. Finally, an inverse analysis framework is developed that uses unsupervised learning-based initialization to accelerate design optimization. This approach substantially accelerates convergence, providing a robust and cost-effective tool for advanced structural design.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Pakistan has experienced an increase in plastic waste generation from domestic consumption and imports from developed countries. Based on the 7th population census (2023), country generates approximately 3.2 million tons (Mt) of plastic waste annually which is projected to reach 4.79 Mt by 2050 at a 1.5% annual growth rate. Due to the limited infrastructure for collection, treatment, and recycling, around 85% of the plastic waste remains mismanaged in urban areas and 100% in rural regions. An estimated 200,000-333,000 waste scavengers serve as the primary recovery mechanism within the informal sector. This study adopts a bottom-up methodology to estimate the plastic waste using the waste amount characterization studies (WACS) from 14 cities. Moreover, assessment of trade, recycling potential, and regulatory frameworks were also discussed. Pakistan imported plastic waste worth of USD 18.77 million in 2024, mainly from the United Kingdom, United Arab Emirates, and the United States. These imports constitute approximately 1.4% of domestic generation showing that the accumulation is largely driven by domestic consumption and inadequate end-of-life management. The analysis distinguishes two policy failure levels. Pakistan has had federal and provincial laws and single-use plastic bans since 1997. The second binding constraint is implementation, with six gaps: no operational Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) system, unharmonized federal and provincial mandates, non-recognition of the informal recovery sector, no collection and recycling infrastructure, weak customs enforcement of Basel-aligned import controls, and no national data Each gap is addressed by enforcement budgets, inter-provincial coordination, waste picker integration, and national monitoring. Adding limits is less credible than sequencing these efforts to satisfy Pakistan’s Basel Convention and Sustainable Development Goals.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Rotary friction welding (RFW) is a solid-state joining process that can bond dissimilar materials with limited melting and short cycle times. This study examines the joining of mild steel rods to alumina (AlO) rods by RFW using an AA1100 aluminium interlayer. The process was carried out in two stages: the interlayer was first formed by friction welding mild steel to aluminium, and the resulting assembly was then friction welded to alumina while the friction time was varied (6, 7, 8 and 9 s) and the remaining parameters were kept constant. The joint interfaces were examined by optical and scanning electron microscopy, the aluminium–alumina interface composition was analysed by energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS), and the mechanical behaviour was assessed by three-point bending and Vickers microhardness measurements. The results indicate that the joint strength depends mainly on the friction time and on the thickness of the residual aluminium interlayer. A longer friction time generated more heat, promoted the penetration of aluminium into the surface pores of the alumina, reduced the residual layer thickness and produced mechanical interlocking at the interface. The highest bending strength, 101.23 MPa, was obtained at the longest friction time (9 s), where the residual layer was thinnest (about 243 m). Within the tested range, the bending strength showed an apparent linear trend with the residual layer thickness (). These observations are consistent with a heat-controlled bonding mechanism, in which the ductile aluminium interlayer wets and mechanically interlocks with the alumina.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: PDF files are primarily intended for human reading rather than automated processing. In addition, the heterogeneous content of PDFs, such as text, tables, and images, poses significant challenges for parsing and information extraction. To address these difficulties, both practitioners and researchers are increasingly developing new methods, including the promising Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems to automated PDF processing. However, there is no comprehensive study investigating how different components and design choices affect the performance of a RAG system for understanding PDFs. In this paper, we propose such a study (1) by focusing on Question Answering, a specific language understanding task, and (2) by leveraging two benchmarks from the financial domain, including TableQuest, our newly generated, publicly available benchmark. We systematically examine multiple PDF parsers and chunking strategies (with varied overlap), along with their potential synergies in preserving document structure and ensuring answer correctness. Overall, our results offer practical guidelines for building robust RAG pipelines for PDF understanding.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Nanomaterial-stabilized Pickering foams are promising alternatives to conventional surfactant foams because solid particles can adsorb at gas-liquid interfaces, reinforce lamellae and Plateau borders, and retard drainage, coalescence, and gas-diffusion-driven coarsening. However, progress remains limited by incomplete links among synthesis, particle descriptors, interfacial organization, foam performance, and application-specific requirements. This review critically examines graphene-based materials, non-graphene carbon nanomaterials, cellulose nanomaterials, and metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), with emphasis on synthesis-controlled properties that govern foam stabilization. Rather than cataloguing preparation methods, oxidation, reduction, exfoliation, functionalization, fibrillation, carbonization, and MOF crystallization or post-synthetic modification are analyzed according to the particle size, morphology, aspect ratio, wettability, surface chemistry, charge, dispersibility, porosity, crystallinity, and surfactant compatibility they generate. The review first establishes the mechanistic basis of surfactant- and particle-stabilized foams, then develops descriptor-mechanism-performance relationships. These relationships connect particle adsorption, interfacial packing, lamella reinforcement, Plateau-border structuring, and bulk-network formation with resistance to drainage, coalescence, and gas transfer. Practical formulation, particle, and operating factors governing the design of stable Pickering foams are critically assessed across the major nanomaterial classes, including particle concentration, dimensionality, size, shape, wettability, surface chemistry, surfactant-particle interactions, additives, salinity, temperature, pressure, and rheological behavior, where relevant evidence is available. Based on quantitative trends reported across the literature, practical design windows are further identified for key formulation and operating variables, providing evidence-informed ranges for material selection while recognizing that the optimum conditions remain system-specific. Graphene-based materials provide extended two-dimensional interfacial coverage and tunable amphiphilicity. Among non-graphene carbon nanomaterials, carbon nanotubes (CNTs) reinforce films and continuous phases through high-aspect-ratio networks, whereas carbon dots contribute through ultrasmall-scale interfacial organization and particle-surfactant coupling. Cellulose nanomaterials offer renewable fibrillar and rod-like structures for drainage resistance and rheological reinforcement. MOFs provide tunable interfacial functionality but remain comparatively underexplored as direct air-water foam stabilizers, with much of the available evidence arising from CO₂/water foams, oil/water Pickering high-internal-phase emulsions (HIPEs), and foam-derived porous architectures. This review directly compares the major nanomaterial classes in terms of dominant stabilization mechanism, operating adaptability, cost, scalability, advantages, limitations, and most suitable applications. Reported applications are organized into enhanced oil recovery and subsurface mobility control, drilling and fracturing fluids, geothermal stimulation, environmental remediation and separation, fluorine-free firefighting, and foam- or HIPE-templated porous materials. Finally, persistent bottlenecks, including narrow formulation windows, aggregation, dynamic-flow instability, synthesis complexity, scale-up, toxicity, nanoparticle release, and secondary-waste handling, are critically evaluated. The review therefore provides an application-driven framework for selecting nanomaterials and defining the mechanistic and engineering evidence required for translation beyond laboratory foam screening.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) have attracted scientists in the field of metallic alloy design due to their noteworthy mechanical and other functional properties. Nevertheless, due to their intricate composition–structure–property relationships, understanding the physical mechanisms using experimental, theoretical, and outdated computational approaches is challenging, as these methods are time-consuming and require extensive computational resources. Recently, machine learning (ML) approaches have gained significant attention for solving these challenges and accelerating the design of HEAs through rapid phase prediction, optimization of alloying elements, and prediction of mechanical and other properties. This review provides a comprehensive overview of ML-driven methodologies for the design and development of various HEAs. The fundamentals of HEAs, including their evolution, core effects, and empirical design approaches using different thermophysical parameters, are discussed first. Subsequently, the application of ML models for phase, mechanical, and functional property prediction is presented, with particular focus on predicting oxidation and corrosion behavior using different ML algorithms. Special emphasis is given to ML-assisted prediction of corrosion- and oxidation-related properties of HEAs, as these properties are important for applications under different environmental conditions. The application of ML in hydrogen storage HEAs, including the prediction of hydrogen storage capacity and hydride formation behavior, is also discussed. Furthermore, the review addresses major challenges in ML, including data availability, data processing, feature engineering, and algorithm interpretability. Finally, future possibilities for ML-based HEA design and combinatorial approaches to accelerate the development of novel HEAs are discussed. In future research, greater importance should be given to standardizing datasets, confirming descriptor uniformity, and integrating CALPHAD/DFT with active ML approaches. The development of physics-guided and multifunctional ML approaches will be useful for exploring phase formation with different compositions and accelerating the discovery of HEAs for specific applications in an accurate manner.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Coupling photocatalytically active semiconductors into a proper heterojunction is attracting significant interest to suppress the recombination of photoinduced electron-hole pairs and enhance photocatalytic performance in degrading organic pollutants. In this study, a novel ternary ZnO/g-C3N4/Bi2S3 Z-scheme heterojunction was successfully synthesized for the first time and investigated via a series of characterization techniques, involving Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), UV-visible spectrophotometer, photoluminescence (PL), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX), and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). The physicochemical results show that the three constituents are homogeneously incorporated into a well-interconnected heterostructure with a high degree of interfacial contact. The ternary nanocomposite demonstrated a highly effective photo-degradation of methylene blue (MB) dye, achieving almost a full MB photodegradation (specifically 99.03%) within only 15 min and with a remarkable kinetic rate constant (k) of 0.2942 min− 1. This performance is considerably superior to that of individual constituents: pure ZnO (87.82%, k = 0.1455 min− 1), g-C3N4 (51.42%, k = 0.0528 min− 1), and Bi2S3 (5.04%, k = 0.0024 min− 1). The superior photo-degradation activity is ascribed to the synergistic effects of its three constituents, boosted photogenerated charges’ separation, and minimized electron-hole recombination. Scavenging experiments and band structure analysis revealed a Z-scheme charge transfer pathway, where Bi2S3 serves as an intermediate electron transfer bridge, and •OH radicals and holes (h+) serve as the primary contributors to photodegradation, followed by •O2− radicals. Crucially, the potential environmental hazard of the nanocomposite was assessed on barley (Hordeum vulgare L.) using random amplified polymorphic DNA-polymerase chain reaction (RAPD-PCR), fluorometric efficacy, and confocal microscopy. These analyses didn’t show phytotoxic, cytotoxic, or genotoxic effects, which confirms the safe use of this novel nanocomposite for real-world environmental remediation. Such a study offers a comprehensive basis for constructing novel nano-based heterostructures for real environmental remediation applications.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: This study investigates the behavior of concrete under impact loading at different temperatures using jacketed piezoelectric sensor (JKTPS) via electro-mechanical impedance (EMI) technique, under both free-free boundary condition (FFBC) and fixed boundary condition (FBC). For this purpose, an experimental study is conducted on concrete cube specimens under FFBC and FBC, where JKTPS configurations were installed to capture the raw signatures (conductance and susceptance vs frequency). The concrete specimens were first preheated to 50 °C, 100 °C, and 150 °C to evaluate temperature effects. Subsequently, an impact load was applied by dropping a free-falling iron ball from a height of 3 m onto the top surface of the specimens. Further, PZT-equivalent stiffness parameters were extracted from the raw signature to identify changes in the specimen’s mechanical properties and to provide a better understanding of various damage conditions. Furthermore, the experimental results from both FFBC and FBC were compared to provide a more accurate assessment of the damage. The experimental results indicate that the concrete cube under FBC experienced a 70 kN/m loss in stiffness, compared to only a 1 kN/m loss under FFBC. This suggests that the FBC sustained significantly more damage, likely due to its higher energy absorption capacity.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: N, N-Dimethylformamide (DMF) and Dichloromethane (DCM) are widely used industrial solvents that pose serious environmental and health risks due to their toxicity and persistence in wastewater. The present study explores the photocatalytic approach for the degradation of DMF and DCM mixture under ultraviolet-visible light irradiation using cerium oxide nanoparticles (CeOx NPs), detached titanium dioxide nanotubes (TiNts), and their hybrid (CeOx/TiNts) nanocatalyst. FESEM, FTIR, Raman, XRD, and TEM indicated that the hybrid nanocatalyst was a mixture of Ce2O3, CeO2 (collectively as CeOx) nanoparticles and TiNts, with a well-crystalline structure, and the CeOx nanoparticles were distributed inside the tubular TiNts. Photocatalytic evaluation of DMF and DCM mixture revealed the DMF degradation efficiencies of 64% for CeOx NPs, 90% for TiNts, and 96% for CeOx/TiNTs, after 120 min of irradiation. The CeOx/TiNts catalyst performed exceptionally as compared to bare CeOx and TiNts, indicating rapid catalytic degradation kinetics attributed to synergistic interaction between CeOx and TiNts by the distribution of Ce₂O₃/CeO₂ across the TiNt surface. It also resulted in enhanced structural integrity and light absorption, thereby improving photocatalytic performance. Gas chromatographic analysis of degraded DCM and DCM mixture revealed a gradual decline in the DMF peak, with no changes in DCM, accompanied by the emergence of volatile intermediates. It indicated the photocatalytic transformation of DMF from a pathway involving C–N bond cleavage and oxidation of intermediates by reactive OH and O₂⁻ species from the hybrid nanocatalyst. Reusability tests revealed that CeOx/TiNts maintained 82% DMF degradation efficiency after the second and 70% after the third cycle. Overall, the results highlight the robustness, selectivity, and recyclability of CeOx/TiNts nanohybrid, emphasizing its potential as a sustainable photocatalyst for wastewater treatment.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Defects such as over-extrusion, stringing, and warping commonly occur in Fused Filament Fabrication (FFF) 3D printing, leading to material waste and substantial time loss when print jobs span several hours. Although supervised computer vision systems can detect specific categories of FFF flaws, they typically require large annotated datasets for each defect type and degrade when the printer, material, or lighting changes, motivating the search for monitoring approaches that rely less on task-specific retraining. This paper presents FA3D, a fault-aware monitoring framework that uses pre-trained Vision-Language Models (VLMs) within an agentic perceive-reason-act loop for zero-shot defect detection on FFF printers. In this work, “fault-aware” refers to the system’s capacity to identify printing faults, evaluate their impact, and trigger appropriate intervention through a VLM-based perception module, a rule-based stop/continue mechanism, and human-in-the-loop decision support. We conduct a comparative zero-shot evaluation of four state-of-the-art VLMs, including Gemini 2.5 Flash Image, GPT-4o, Qwen 2.5-VL-32B, and GLM-4.5V, on a balanced dataset of 140 print images, and analyze precision, recall, F1-score, and F2-score, where the F2-score is emphasized to reflect the higher cost of missed defects. Gemini 2.5 Flash Image achieves the best overall performance with an F2-score of 0.901 and a recall of 97.1%, while GPT-4o reaches 100% recall at the cost of frequent false alarms, and GLM-4.5V reaches perfect precision but misses 63.8% of defects. The study positions VLM-based zero-shot monitoring as a practical complement to supervised detectors for low-volume and rapidly changing print scenarios, while clearly delineating its current limitations in terms of dataset breadth, prompt sensitivity, and dependence on external APIs.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: The interplay between structural chirality and the optoelectronic characteristics of two-dimensional (2D) materials has emerged as a frontier in modern science, opening pathways to novel technologies. Among these, the chiral-induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect— where chiral structures enable spin-polarized charge transport without external magnetic fields—holds promising potential for advancing spintronics and optoelectronics. Despite its promise, the precise mechanism of the CISS effect remains uncertain. This review provides a comprehensive and critical assessment of the CISS effect in chiral 2D materials, bridging fundamental principles with emerging applications. We first discuss the proposed mechanisms behind CISS, including spin-dependent electron transport and spin polarization via charge displacement, along with competing theoretical models. We then critically evaluate the suite of theoretical and experimental techniques for characterizing CISS, discussing their strengths and limitations. Subsequently, we present the latest advances in chiral 2D materials, focusing on their chirality transfer mechanisms and resultant spin-polarization capabilities—insights pivotal for designing next-generation spin-based optoelectronic devices. Building on these foundations, we explore the state-of-the-art spintronic applications, while offering a critical analysis of the underlying physics and chemistry. Finally, we identify key challenges and propose a roadmap for future research and innovation in this dynamic field.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: This study investigates the leaching of phosphate ore in a mixed hydrochloric (HCl)-perchloric (HClO4) system to optimize and determine the kinetics of the reaction. The raw, calcined, and leached samples were analyzed using X-Ray Fluorescence (XRF), X-Ray Diffraction (XRD), and Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) to determine the chemical composition, mineral phases, and surface morphology. A Box–Behnken design under Response Surface Methodology (RSM) was applied to evaluate the effects of temperature (°C), acid concentration (M), and reaction time (min) on phosphate leaching efficiency, and shrinking models were tested to study the kinetics of the reaction. The XRF results showed that CaO (61.966%) and P2O5 (16.929 %) in the calcined phosphate ore reduced drastically to 7.51 % and 1.28 % after leaching, while Fe2O3 and SiO2 increased to 47.31 % and 26.97 %, confirming selective phosphate leaching. XRD analysis revealed the disappearance of apatite peaks and the emergence of quartz and hematite phases, while SEM showed porous, corroded surfaces in the leached residue. Within the selected RSM design space, the optimum condition was identified as 50 °C, 0.5 M HCl-HClO4, and 60 min. At this condition, the highest experimental response in the Box–Behnken design matrix was 97.0%, the model-predicted dissolution efficiency was 96.25%, and the independent validation experiment gave 95.5%. Kinetic analysis showed that the dissolution process was best described by the surface chemical reaction control model among the shrinking-core models evaluated, with an apparent reaction order of 0.478 with respect to acid concentration. The apparent activation energy was estimated as 16.11 kJ mol−1.

Attacks such as denial-of-service, reply, and deception are all examined concurrently because fuzzy networked systems are vulnerable. Initially, a non-fragile event-triggered control mechanism is described, and mathematically demonstrated to be free of the Zeno phenomenon, to minimise the bandwidth used during attacks in the additional control loop. As a result, communication resources can be preserved and the frequency of event triggers can be decreased. Using the Lyapunov-Krsovskii functional, we detect an adequate condition to ensure asymptotic stability in the closed-loop system. The observer gain matrix and the controller gain matrix are obtained using the linear matrix inequalities approach. Lastly, the efficacy of the proposed technique is demonstrated using the simulation findings.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Drone light shows (DLShows) represent a rapidly growing application of swarm robotics, creating captivating aerial displays through the synchronized flight of hundreds or thousands of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) as environmentally friendly and reusable alternatives to traditional pyrotechnics. This domain presents unique challenges in optimally assigning drones to visual waypoints and generating smooth, collision-free trajectories at a very large scale. This article introduces the Unified Assignment and Trajectory Generation (UATG) framework. The proposed approach concurrently solves two core problems: the optimal assignment of drones to designated goal locations and the generation of dynamically feasible, collision-free, time-parameterized trajectories. The UATG framework is specifically designed for DLShows, ensuring minimal transition times between formations and guaranteeing inter-drone collision avoidance. A key innovation is its exceptional computational efficiency, enabling the coordination of large-scale in real-time; for instance, it computes the optimal assignment and trajectories for 1008 drones in approximately 1 s on a standard laptop. Extensive simulations in realistic environments validate the framework's performance, demonstrating its capability to orchestrate complex formations—from alphanumeric characters to intricate 3D shapes—with precision and visual smoothness. This work provides a critical advancement for the DLShow industry, offering a practical and scalable solution for generating complex aerial choreography and establishing a valuable benchmark for ground control station software designed for the efficient coordination of multiple UAVs. mods:mods.mods:abstract: The mobility and safety benefits of Connected and Automated vehicles (CAVs) are an ongoing area of research. While several studies demonstrate the advantages of CAVs, there remains a gap in quantifying these benefits over conventional Automated Vehicles (AVs). Roadworks (RWs) are particularly challenging driving environment for AVs/CAVs. This paper evaluates the safety and mobility benefits of CAVs over AVs in RW conditions. The primary focus is on examining the lane change behaviour of AVs/CAVs at different design speeds, specifically 40 km/h, 60 km/h, and 80 km/h. A simulated environment is developed to integrate CAVs and RW areas featuring lane closure. To achieve this, state-of-the-art models (lateral behaviour: Minimising Overall Braking Induced by Lane Changes (MOBIL); and longitudinal behaviour: Intelligent Driver Model (IDM)) were utilised, incorporating improvements to simulate near misses and crashes incidents. Furthermore, the study delves into the crucial aspect of safety by investigating the effects of model parameters on the chances of traffic crashes. The research findings demonstrate that CAVs start lane change manoeuvre early, particularly under high traffic flow conditions. Specifically, at a speed of 40 km/h and under high traffic conditions, CAVs demonstrated a success rate ranging from 91% to 96%, while AVs exhibited a substantially lower success rate, ranging only between 10% and 11%. The simulation results further highlight a lack of collisions in AVs/CAVs during lane change at RW. This research serves as a valuable contribution to the field of automated driving, providing insights into the optimisation of lane change behaviours and safety considerations at RW environments.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: We investigate how cooperation evolves in multiplayer games on regular graphs of degree k when individuals base their decisions on both their own aspiration levels and the success of their neighbors. We calculate explicit first-order formulas for fixation probabilities using pair approximation and diffusion methods under weak selection. These formulas separate aspiration effects from payoff effects filtered by the graph. We show that increasing the graph degree attenuates the selection effects driven by payoffs. In contrast, the contribution of the aspiration gap Δα=αD−αC is independent of graph degree at first order. We apply the framework to public goods, stag-hunt, and snowdrift games and obtain corresponding conditions for the evolutionary success of cooperation. In the public goods and stag-hunt games, the conditions at large degree retain cost terms, so cooperation requires a sufficiently positive aspiration gap to compensate for the cost of contributing. In the snowdrift game, both benefit and cost contributions vanish in the high-degree limit, leaving the aspiration gap as the leading first-order contribution. Monte Carlo simulations on connected random regular graphs of degree k are consistent with the first-order predictions within their formal regime of validity, while simulations outside this regime are interpreted only as qualitative checks of the predicted trends.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: This study examines whether financial inclusion strategies in faith-based charity organisations are shaped primarily by executive dispositions or by governance authority structures. Drawing on upper echelons and agency theories, it develops an integrated framework explaining variation in the formalisation of resource redistribution through banking channels. Financial inclusion is viewed as a strategic mechanism through which organisations facilitate participation in the formal financial system by connecting beneficiaries to regulated financial institutions. The evidence shows that leadership characteristics exert a systematic influence on the adoption of such strategies. Specifically, organisations led by female, altruistic, and younger chief executives are significantly more likely to channel resources through formal financial institutions, whereas governance arrangements that concentrate managerial authority are associated with lower levels of strategic formalisation. Additional analyses indicate that the influence of female leadership is amplified in the presence of larger and more gender-diverse boards. Collectively, the results suggest that financial inclusion strategies are driven more strongly by executive values and cognitive orientations than by governance-based authority alone. The study contributes to the literature on leadership, governance, financial inclusion, and the third sector by demonstrating that executive characteristics represent a critical organisational mechanism through which broader participation in formal financial systems is achieved.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Early-age thermal cracking in mass concrete due to cement hydration heat increases maintenance and energy demands, motivating reliable prediction and control of hydration exotherm in polymer-modified systems. This study develops a hybrid thermo-kinetic deep learning framework that couples equivalent-age normalization, stretched-exponential hydration kinetics, isothermal calorimetry, and physics-regularized recurrent neural networks (RNN) with copolymer descriptors for styrene-co-butylacrylate-co-2-ethylhexylacrylate-co-methylmethacrylate (St-co-BA-co-EHA-co-MMA) modified cement. mods:mods.mods:abstract: Writer identification in historical Arabic manuscripts supports manuscript authentication, cataloging, and cultural heritage preservation, yet progress is constrained by the scarcity of reliable writerlabeled datasets. This paper introduces Writer Identification in Historical Arabic Manuscripts (WrIHAM), a curated dataset of 62 handwritten books by 18 known writers, comprising 1,144 pages, with an average of 3.44 books per writer. Each writer is represented by at least three manuscripts, and domain experts reviewed the attribution of each book. The dataset spans the 11th to 17th centuries of the Common Era (CE) and captures substantial variation in handwriting, page condition, layout, and scanning quality. We evaluated writer identification under a realistic manuscript-level generalization setting using book-disjoint training, validation, and test splits, which prevent document-level leakage and require the model to generalize to entirely unseen manuscripts. To evaluate the suitability of our dataset, we compared two strong deep learning backbones: EfficientNet-B4 and a Data-efficient Image Transformer (DeiT) model, specifically DeiT-Base- Patch16-224. Both models were evaluated under book-disjoint and book-shared protocols using a line-based pipeline with page-level aggregation. The results show that the evaluation protocol has a major effect on performance: although the book-shared protocol yields near-ceiling accuracy, the realistic book-disjoint setting remains substantially more challenging. Under the book-disjoint protocol, DeiT achieved the best mean macro-averaged page-level top-1 accuracy of 60.1%, compared with 56.4% for EfficientNet-B4. These results establish WrIHAM as a challenging benchmark for realistic writer identification in historical Arabic manuscripts.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: This paper proposes a multi-stage control strategy for quadcopter trajectory tracking under wind disturbances and payload variations. The approach is built on a standard cascaded architecture, where the outer loop regulates horizontal position and generates attitude references, while the inner loop tracks the commanded attitudes. First, particle swarm optimization (PSO) is implemented offline to tune baseline PID controllers for the outer-loop horizontal channels and inner-loop attitude channels using a tracking-based objective function. Then, a supervisory fuzzy self-tuning mechanism is integrated within the inner loop to adapt the attitude PID gains online according to the tracking error and its rate, improving robustness against coupling effects and external disturbances. To ensure effective and bounded adaptation, a genetic algorithm (GA) is employed offline to optimize the fuzzy scaling factors. In addition, Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Control (LADRC) is assigned to the altitude channel to explicitly address payload-induced thrust-to-weight mismatch by estimating and compensating for the total disturbance. MATLAB/Simulink simulations demonstrate improved trajectory tracking and disturbance rejection compared with the PSO-tuned fixed-gain baseline. Performance evaluation using the integral of time-weighted absolute error (ITAE) confirms superior robustness under wind disturbance and payload variation scenarios while maintaining bounded control effort.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Constructing crystalline chiral covalent organic frameworks (CCOFs) with programmable chiroptical properties from a single chiral source remains highly challenging. Herein, we report a dynamic covalent evolution strategy that transforms supramolecular-induced helical covalent organic polymers into mesoscopic helical CCOFs through thermodynamic self-crystallization as well as single-step and stepwise monomer exchange. Remarkably, two distinct chiroptical inversion modes are preserved during framework evolution: a conventional inversion accompanied by opposite helical sense and a second inversion displaying opposite chiroptical activity despite identical mesoscopic helicity, originating from different sub-nanometer chiral packing arrangements. Time-dependent experiments and theoretical calculations reveal persistent chirality- and packing-memory effects throughout dynamic reconstruction. Using a single chiral template system, this strategy affords 24 mesoscopic helical CCOFs with diverse linkage chemistries and programmable chiroptical responses. Furthermore, pore-confined incorporation of aggregation-induced emissive guests extends both inversion modes into flexible circularly polarized luminescence films.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Investments are the foundation of financial markets, directing resources toward activities that generate future returns. Stock trading plays a central role in wealth creation, yet forecasting stock prices remains difficult due to the nonlinear and volatile nature of financial data. This study presents an ensemble deep learning framework for short-term stock price forecasting in the Saudi market. It addresses the limited use of advanced ensemble methods in emerging economies. The framework uses multivariate data from ten companies listed on the Tadawul All Share Index and compares two ensemble strategies: averaging and stacking with standalone models (Gated Recurrent Unit, Long Short-Term Memory, and Bidirectional Recurrent Neural Network). A total of 34 engineered technical indicators and a rolling-window setup were applied for five-day-ahead predictions. The results show that ensemble models consistently outperform individual architectures across all evaluation metrics. Stacking ensembles, especially those combining Gated Recurrent Unit and Long Short-Term Memory, achieved the highest accuracy. Averaging ensembles provided stable and efficient alternatives. Overall, the findings confirm the robustness and adaptability of ensemble methods for financial forecasting and offer practical insights for investors and policymakers seeking reliable, data-driven prediction tools.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: H2- and He-broadening coefficients of CO2 and their temperature dependence were measured for the R(18) and R(20) transitions of the ν1+ν3 band at 3728.4101 and 3729.7122 cm−1, respectively. Measurements were performed using a tunable distributed-feedback laser near 2.7 µm in a high-temperature optical cell. Absorbance spectra were recorded for mixtures of 1–4% CO2 in H2 or He at ten pressures between 75 and 600 Torr, covering temperatures of 295–805 K for H2 and 295–1005 K for He. The upper temperature limit for the H2 mixtures was imposed by the onset of the reverse water-gas shift reaction. The measured line shapes were fitted with Voigt profiles, with residuals typically less than 1%. Broadening coefficients were obtained from the linear pressure dependence of the fitted collisional widths, and temperature exponents were obtained from power-law fits. The room-temperature H2-broadening coefficients are 0.1124 and 0.1118 cm−1 atm−1 for the R(18) and R(20) transitions, with temperature exponents of 0.676 and 0.655, respectively. The corresponding He-broadening coefficients are 0.0591 and 0.0583 cm−1 atm−1, with exponents of 0.569 and 0.543. The measured H2 exponents are 13–16% larger than the constant value adopted in HITRAN 2024 but agree within 6% with recent requantized classical molecular dynamics predictions. These results provide the first H2- and He-broadening data for the ν1+ν3 band and the first experimental validation of He-broadening predictions above 760 K.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: With the growing reliance of multi-area interconnected power systems on communication networks for large-scale data transmission, sensing, and control, network constraints can impair transient performance. This work develops a unified distributed fault-estimation framework based on a radial basis function neural network (RBF-NN) for multi-area interconnected power systems, addressing both communication constraints and actuator faults. We construct an augmented system by integrating the fault dynamics into the system model, and a distributed observer is developed to simultaneously estimate the system states and fault dynamics. The unknown fault effect is approximated by a radial basis function neural network (RBF-NN). A projection-based adaptation law ensures bounded parameter estimation under modeling uncertainties. State and fault estimates are updated using quantized measurements transmitted over networked channels, maintaining accuracy despite time-varying delays and disturbances. Sufficient stability and performance conditions are established by Lyapunov analysis and LMI conditions, guaranteeing exponential stability of the observer error dynamics and prescribed performance bounds under bounded time-varying delays and quantization effects. A three-area case study is presented, and precise state and fault reconstruction are shown for nominal, delayed, faulted, and worst-case scenarios. The proposed scheme is compared with a quantized H∞ estimator under actuator faults, time-varying delays, and quantization. The peak deviations of |Δω|, |ΔPtie|, and |ΔPmech| are reduced approximately 33%, 50%, and 27%, respectively, while maintaining bounded system states and neural weights.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: A high-throughput ab-initio framework is used to identify two-dimensional materials suitable for thermoelectric applications. Out of 290 experimentally exfoliable materials, a total of 150 monolayers are selected through band gap screening. For these, we compute the thermoelectric transport coefficients and power factor scaled by the relaxation time, S2σ/τ, finding that most of them exceed 5 × 1011 W/mKs. Further screening is then applied by using the average atomic weight criterion. It is found that the p-type monolayers with high S2σ/τ are mostly tetradymites, such as Sb2SeTe2, Bi2STe2, and Bi2SeTe2, except for the less known Sb2SnTe4. In contrast, n-type monolayers with high S2σ/τ are found over a wider range of structures, although typically their S2σ/τ is lower than that of the p-type monolayers. The five best-performing p-type and n-type monolayers are selected for studying their electronic and phonon transport properties. The electronic relaxation time is computed from the electron-phonon coupling matrix, while the lattice thermal conductivity is calculated from the ab-initio force constants up to the third order. Sb2SeTe2 is predicted to provide a high power factor of 26 mW/mK2, while GeTe and Sb2SnTe4 show at 300 K ultra low lattice thermal conductivities of 0.34 and 0.46 W/mK, respectively. Overall the conducted large-scale screening exercise allows us to identify both p-type and n-type monolayers with excellent thermoelectric performance in terms of the figure of merit.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Introduction – Remote sensing image classification is an important task in Earth observation. However, achieving high accuracy is still challenging. This is mainly due to high-dimensional feature redundancy, large intra-class variability, and the difficulty of capturing both fine spatial details and long-range contextual information. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a unified classification framework based on a novel Multi-Scale Dual-Path Shifted Pyramid Vision Transformer (M-DSPViT). Methods – The proposed model improves standard Vision Transformer architectures by introducing dual-path shifted patch embedding and content-adaptive attention gating. It also incorporates multi-scale feature pyramid fusion, dynamic expert routing, and gradient-based attention masking to better capture spatial and contextual features. In addition, a hybrid feature selection method (HSIC-HFS) is introduced to remove redundant information and retain discriminative features. This method combines the Hilbert-Schmidt independence criterion, Shannon entropy, and L 1-regularization. The refined features are then integrated with CNN-based spatial descriptors extracted using EfficientNet through a Sequential Feature Aggregation (SFA) framework. Results – The proposed method is evaluated on the WHU-RS19, UC Merced, and AID benchmark datasets. It achieves state-of-the-art performance in land-use classification. The robustness and generalization ability of the model are further validated through statistical analysis, including one-way ANOVA and F-statistic testing. Discussion – The results confirm the stability of the proposed approach across different remote sensing scenarios.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: The increasing frequency and intensity of typhoons in recent years due to climate change has heightened the need for rapid post-disaster assessment. Inspection of post-typhoon damage is required to assess damages to critical infrastructure and facilitate disaster management. Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are commonly used for the recognition of post-typhoon damage. However, existing UAVs require either to be manually teleoperated or to follow a pre-programmed flight path, which is significantly limited in terms of rapid or adaptive post-typhoon inspection. To address this critical limitation, this study introduces a novel agentic AI and aerial robotics-enabled model designed for autonomous inspection operations. We propose a three-layered conceptual framework that closes the perception–cognition–action loop, thereby enabling goal-directed mission reasoning. This framework is operationalized as the Agentic AI and UAV-enabled Autonomous Inspection and Assessment System (AAUIAS)—a comprehensive cyber-physical system architecture. Within this architecture, the core agentic AI layer independently performs world modeling, real-time damage assessment, and dynamic path replanning. The proposed model and system were evaluated through high-fidelity simulations of a typhoon-impacted urban environment. Results demonstrate that AAUIAS reduces overall inspection time by 34.5%–40.2% relative to conventional approaches, achieves robust dynamic obstacle avoidance, and intelligently prioritizes critical damage sites. This preliminary work contributes a conceptual model and system architecture, supported by simulation-based evidence, for transforming UAVs into proactive intelligent agents, thereby advancing the state of the art in autonomous disaster response and resilient infrastructure management.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Purpose – This study aims to examine the symmetric and asymmetric effects of exchange rate changes and exchange rate volatility on domestic investment in G7 economies. It investigates whether currency appreciations and depreciations and increases and decreases in volatility exert differential short-run and long-run effects on investment. Design/methodology/approach – Using quarterly data from 1973Q1–2024Q4, the study applies linear autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) and nonlinear ARDL (NARDL) models. The NARDL framework captures asymmetries by decomposing exchange rate changes and volatility into positive and negative components. Volatility is measured using generalized autoregressive conditional heteroskedasticity (1, 1), with robustness checked using an eight-quarter rolling standard deviation. Structural breaks are controlled through country-specific dummy variables. Findings – Linear ARDL results show that exchange rate changes affect short-run investment in most G7 economies, with long-run effects in Canada, Germany, the UK and the USA. Volatility reduces long-run investment in France, Japan and the USA. NARDL results reveal significant short- and long-run asymmetries. Appreciations raise investment in Canada but reduce it in France and Japan, while depreciations lower investment in Germany, the UK and the USA but increase it in Italy. Rising volatility boosts investment in Japan and the UK but reduces it in France and the USA. These findings are robust to alternative volatility measures. Originality/value – This study is the first to jointly model exchange rate and volatility asymmetries within a unified NARDL framework for the G7. Extending the sample through 2024 and confirming robustness across alternative volatility measures provides more comprehensive evidence than single-channel studies.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Text mining helps researchers extract meaningful insights from large amounts of unstructured text. This study reviews how text mining has been used in operations management (OM) and engineering management (EM) research between 2011 and 2025, with a focus on articles published in leading journals in both fields. Our review shows that the use of text mining has increased rapidly in recent years, reflecting its growing importance as a research tool. A central contribution of this study is the development of step by step guidelines for applying text mining in OM and EM research. These guidelines cover the full research process, including data collection, preprocessing, feature extraction and selection, modeling, interpretation, and validation. The review also examines two major challenges in current applications: sentiment analysis and topic modeling. In both areas, researchers often face problems such as semantic ambiguity and model instability, which can reduce the reliability and interpretability of findings. To address these issues, we review and recommend approaches such as stable latent Dirichlet allocation and aspect-based sentiment analysis, drawing on established literature to identify methods that can improve analytical robustness. Overall, this review offers both researchers and practitioners a practical resource for applying text mining more effectively, consistently, and with greater confidence in OM and EM contexts.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Digital transformation (DT) has been widely acknowledged for its potential to promote social sustainability practice (SSP). As the world's primary manufacturing center, China has witnessed rapid adoption of DT; nevertheless, lingering social sustainability issues have exposed a significant gap in research on how such transformation drives the diffusion of SSP along supply chains. To address this research gap, this study employs fixed effects regression and difference-in-differences analysis using panel data from 2750 Chinese manufacturing firms and 186 buyer–supplier dyads from 2011 to 2021. Grounded in the knowledge diffusion perspective, the study identifies that DT exerts a positive effect on the SSP of both focal firms and their suppliers, while supplier SSP mediates the link between buyer DT and buyer SSP. Furthermore, high buyer power attenuates the reverse diffusion pathway of SSP from suppliers to buyer firms. These findings are further validated by difference-in-differences estimation. By framing DT as an enabler of SSP-related knowledge transfer and power asymmetry as a barrier to reverse knowledge flows from suppliers to buyers, this study deepens theoretical understanding and offers practical implications for industry practitioners.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Artificial Intelligence Customer Service (AICS) is increasingly being adopted by online platforms to enhance efficiency, yet consumer automation aversion creates significant strategic challenges. AICS adoption strategies within a platform supply chain, featuring one platform and two competing manufacturers, are investigated in this study. Using a game-theoretic model, we analyze how the platform's strategic use of a per-unit AICS usage fee interacts with manufacturer competition and consumer aversion. The analysis reveals several critical, counterintuitive findings. First, under unilateral adoption, a higher AICS usage fee can paradoxically incentivize greater platform investment, leading to a tripartite win-win. This occurs because the fee acts as a strategic commitment device. Second, this mechanism vanishes under symmetric bilateral adoption, where the fee reverts to a conventional marginal cost, making a win-win outcome highly restrictive. Third, the extension to asymmetric competition uncovers a complex U-shaped incentive for adoption: both cost-advantaged and cost-disadvantaged firms strategically avoid bilateral competition when their costs fall into an intermediate range. This research reframes the AICS usage fee as a strategic lever for incentive alignment, rather than merely a cost, and establishes consumer aversion as a critical moderator of all strategic outcomes. Our findings provide crucial insights for platforms and manufacturers navigating the trade-offs between AI's potential, competitive dynamics, and consumer psychology.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices have increasingly garnered attention on a global scale, highlighting the importance of understanding the potential consequences of ESG performance. The objective of this study is to examine the impact of a firm’s ESG performance on the behaviors of suppliers, with a particular emphasis on the trade credit provided by these suppliers. Furthermore, this research also analyzes operations and supply chain management (OSCM) factors such as operational efficiency (OE), supplier concentration (SC), and R&D intensity (R&D), which may serve to moderate this relationship. To achieve these goals, we perform a secondary data analysis encompassing 2,046 listed companies in Chinese manufacturing industries from 2018 to 2023 and find that the performance of corporations in terms of ESG displays an inverted U-shaped correlation with trade credit. Moreover, OE and R&D intensity steepen the inverted U-shape and shift the turning point to the left, while SC flattens the inverted U-shape and also shifts the turning point to the left. These findings suggest that ESG has important logistics and supply chain consequences because it shapes suppliers’ willingness to provide the short-term financing that helps stabilize procurement, production, and delivery activities. In light of these findings, we provide a noteworthy contribution to the existing literature on buyer–supplier relationships and logistics fulfilment presenting important implications for both researchers and practitioners in the domain of OSCM.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Purpose – This study aims to systematically evaluate and compare existing neighborhood-level social sustainability assessment tools (SSATs) by examining their hierarchical indicator structure, coverage, level of convergence and representational balance to evaluate their ability to represent and measure the multidimensional construct of social sustainability. Design/methodology/approach – A structured coverage analysis was conducted on 23 neighborhood-level SSATs, including 19 academically developed tools and four widely used formal rating systems (LEED for Neighborhood Development, BREEAM Communities, MOSTADAM Communities and LEED for Cities and Communities). Through an iterative content analysis process at the operational level of the indicator, a total of 605 indicator instances were extracted, of which 213 were unique indicators, grouped into six categories and 18 subcategories, forming the Comprehensive Social Sustainability Assessment Framework (CSSAF). Breadth and depth of coverage were examined against CSSAF at the category, subcategory and indicator levels. Convergence among tools was quantified using vector-based weighted Jaccard similarity. Findings – Results reveal weak convergence across neighborhood-level SSATs. Approximately 83% of CSSAF indicators appear in only one or two tools, and no tool covers more than 78% of CSSAF subcategories. Similarity analysis further confirms substantial fragmentation among tools (mean J = 0.096; median J = 0.091), with many tool pairs demonstrating near-zero overlap. Coverage is also systematically imbalanced, with indicators concentrated on livability-related dimensions, particularly access to amenities/services and housing, while urban integration and governance-related dimensions, such as community resilience, external integration and civic engagement, remain consistently underrepresented. Formal rating systems provide more standardized and auditable assessment structures but generally capture a narrower portion of the social sustainability construct, as defined by CSSAF, compared with academically developed tools. Originality/value – This study develops a traceable consolidated framework (CSSAF) and provides a comprehensive set of coverage metrics that can diagnose the comprehensiveness, representativeness, convergence and structural consistency of existing neighborhood-level (SSATs). The resulting framework supports more transparent tool selection, identification of systematic underrepresentation and coverage gaps, and development of more balanced and context-sensitive social sustainability assessment systems.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Purpose – Digital transformation (DT) research remains fragmented as prior studies adopt linear and factor-based approaches that overlook causal complexity. Drawing on the configurational theory and critical realism, this study addresses whether and how multiple organizational conditions combine to shape DT outcomes in an emerging economy. Design/methodology/approach – We employ qualitative comparative analysis (QCA) analysis to examine interview data from 27 firms in Vietnam's manufacturing industry to identify causal configurations associated with high and low DT. Findings – Results reveal multiple equifinal pathways to high and low DT, demonstrating causal asymmetry. Managerial motivation and strategic alignment are necessary conditions but remain insufficient alone, requiring complementary capabilities such as change management and technological infrastructure for high DT. Asymmetrical analyses show that low DT reflects cumulative capability deficiencies rather than simple absence of successful conditions. Practical implications – Managers should diagnose firm-specific capability bundles, align leadership and strategy, strengthen complementary capabilities and address barriers before scaling resource-sensitive DT initiatives. Originality/value – This study advances DT literature by: (1) theorizing DT as configurational and context-contingent rather than linear and (2) showing how complementary mechanisms intertwined generate multiple pathways to high and low DT in an emerging manufacturing context.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Rapid and accurate assessment of bacterial concentration is essential, yet conventional methods remain constrained by low detection sensitivity at low concentrations with long processing times. Optical density (OD₆₂₅) measurements report a detection sensitivity value of approximately of 93% for high concentrations of CFU/mL. Plate count assays under similar bacteria parameters exhibit 62% and require > 24 h for incubation and colony enumeration. In this study, we introduce the dielectrophoretic (DEP)-based crossover frequency (fx0) method as a quantitative, frequency-based metric for rapid bacterial concentration assessment, varying concentrations of initial, 1:10, 1:100, and 1:1000 representing bacteria parameter of. The initial concentration, 1.5 × 10⁸ CFU mL, yielded an OD₆₂₅ of 0.12, an average plate count of 320 CFU, and an fx0 of 4.5 MHz, corresponding to the densest bacterial population. At a 1:10 concentration, these values decreased to OD₆₂₅ = 0.08, 220 CFU, andfx0 = 3.23 MHz. Further dilution to 1:100 concentration yielded OD₆₂₅ = 0.05, 186 CFU, and fx0 = 2.50 MHz, while the most dilute sample at 1:1000 concentration showed OD₆₂₅ = 0.011, 80 CFU, and fx0 = 0.71 MHz, reflecting reduced cell density and conductivity. Detection sensitivity analysis from the response normalization equation for OD₆₂₅, plate count, and fx0 experimental achieved values of 53.6%, 59.15%, and 60.69%, respectively. Based on the increasing trend of OD₆₂₅, plate count, and DEP-based fx0 values with respect to each method, we plotted a linear fit, OD₆₂₅ (R2 = 0.963), plate count (R2 = 0.949) and DEP-based fx0 (R2 = 0.981). The plotted line serves as a reference for the expected values of OD₆₂₅, plate count, and DEP-based fx0 at the selected medium conductivity (σₘ) for the following evaluation tests. We introduced high σₘ values of 0.8 S/m, 0.6 S/m, 0.4 S/m, and 0.2 S/m, and low σₘ values of 0.08 S/m, 0.06 S/m, 0.04 S/m, and 0.02 S/m in the evaluation test to observe the deviation between the plotted line of the expected trend and the actual measured values. We calculated the deviations between expected and measured values and produced a mean deviation of 116% for OD₆₂₅, 49% for plate count, and 60% for DEP-based fx0 with p < 0.05, indicating a strong linear relationship between expected values and actual values measured of every method, thus demonstrating trend agreement within the tested conductivity range, while also revealing nonlinear deviations at elevated conductivity. mods:mods.mods:abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable infrastructure has prompted research into alternative materials that can replace conventional, environmentally detrimental components in construction. This study proposes a novel waste expanded polystyrene (WEPS) based polymer binder that completely replaces conventional petroleum asphalt binder, representing an alternative binding concept rather than a conventional polymer-modified asphalt system. The mechanical performance of the WEPS-based mixture was evaluated and compared to traditional asphalt binder mixtures through a series of standardized tests, including compressive strength, dynamic creep, indirect tensile fatigue, resilient modulus, indirect tensile strength, and volumetric analysis. Results revealed that the WEPS-based binder improved the mechanical performance of the pavement mixture. Specifically, the WEPS mixture exhibited a compressive strength of 40.79 MPa, over 4.5 times that of the asphalt mixture. Dynamic creep results showed minimal permanent deformation in the WEPS mixture (1053 µm vs. 16,560 µm), indicating higher rutting resistance. The fatigue life was greatly extended in the WEPS-based mixture, with negligible deformation over 28,334 cycles, highlighting its durability under repeated loading. Furthermore, the WEPS mixture demonstrated a resilient modulus up to 24.24 MPa and indirect tensile strength of 6461.5 kPa, showing much stronger performance compared to the traditional asphalt mixture. Volumetric analysis confirmed the lightweight nature of the WEPS binder, resulting in slightly higher air voids and VMA. The WEPS-based mixture offers lower cost and energy use but results in slightly higher CO₂ emissions compared to the asphalt binder mixture. This proposed approach not only addresses the challenge of plastic waste disposal but also contributes to the development of high-performance, sustainable pavement materials.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Estimating strong motion parameters in shallow geological formations is crucial in seismic hazard assessment and earthquake engineering, which can be achieved through the development of Ground Motion Models (GMMs). These parameters provide essential information for designing earthquake-resistant structures and infrastructure. Accelerometer networks may cover diverse geological settings and therefore require comprehensive site characterization for reliable ground motion recordings. In this study, Crete Island in Greece was selected as a region prone to seismic hazards for the subsurface characterization of 13 accelerometer sites located along the island by integrating surface and borehole geological and geophysical data from Spectral and Multichannel Surface Waves Analysis (SASW & MASW), Refraction Microtremor (ReMi or MAM-Microtremor Array Measurement), Seismic Refraction Tomography and Electrical Resistivity Tomography (SRT & ERT). This research resulted in the estimation of several geophysical and geotechnical parameters, such as the P and S-wave velocity, the Young's modulus, the Poisson's ratio and the maximum shear modulus. Based on these parameters, engineers can estimate strong motion intensity measures on the surface, using corresponding values on engineering bedrock. The resulting velocity and impedance models provide physically based constraints on site amplification, high-frequency attenuation, and basin effects, supporting future development of site-specific and non-ergodic GMMs. Thus, the dynamic properties of shallow geological formations may rationally serve in understanding effects of subsurface complexity structure. In addition, strong ground motion recordings in the characterized stations may be effectively utilized for hosting to target sites (Host To Target Adjustment: HTTA). The area investigated comprises a variety of geological and tectonic settings, making it an ideal location for investigating the effects of different geological conditions on ground motion intensity measures. This study provides a methodological example for the refinement of the geological model of a site by integrating surface high-resolution geological mapping, geophysical imaging, and borehole validation. The findings of this work indicate that the methods used in this study contributed to the mapping of different physical properties in different depth ranges. MASW and SRT provided the shallow S- and P-wave velocity structure, respectively, which affects the high-frequency ground motion, while Ambient Vibration Arrays (AVA) mapped deeper seismic impedance contrasts that control long-period seismic response. ERT is a valuable tool for estimating a formation's lithology and heterogeneity, but it cannot directly quantify its mechanical properties. Finally, borehole and in-situ geotechnical tests provided high vertical resolution information and guided geophysical data interpretation. By the integration of these complementary methods, we achieved the evaluation of a scale-consistent and realistic site subsurface model.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Reinforced concrete underpins infrastructure, yet steel corrosion shortens its service life and threatens public safety. This study presents a multiscale mechanistic investigation of sodium metasilicate (SM, Na2SiO3) as a corrosion inhibitor for C1018 carbon steel in chloride-contaminated simulated concrete pore solution (SCPS) (pH > 12.6, 3.5 wt.% NaCl), combining electrochemical measurements, surface characterization, and DFT/MD simulations. This work advances the field through three novel contributions: (i) an optimal low-concentration regime (305 ppm) under severe chloride exposure without co-inhibitors, in contrast to prior studies using high SM dosages or mild chloride conditions; (ii) atomistic insight into the adsorption behavior of SM in SCPS through complementary DFT and MD simulations; and (iii) resolution of the protection mechanism as adsorption-assisted surface stabilization rather than passive-film formation. Across five concentrations (38–610 ppm), electrochemical analysis reveals a non-monotonic concentration-efficiency relationship, yielding inhibition efficiencies of 92.6% (LPR) and 89.9% (PDP). Impedance spectroscopy attributes this protection mainly to a sharp rise in charge-transfer resistance, consistent with adsorption-controlled inhibition. Tafel analysis confirms mixed-type inhibition with anodic predominance. SEM, EDS, and 3D profilometry show reduced surface degradation, lower roughness ( Sa : 0.119 vs. 0.212 μm; Sq : 0.153 vs. 0.293 μm), and Ca-rich interfacial deposits, with silicon detected only in trace amounts, supporting adsorption-assisted stabilization rather than indicating the formation of a continuous Si-rich barrier. DFT calculations identify the silicate anion’s oxygen atoms as the dominant electron-donating sites (HOMO: −4.439 eV; ΔE = 3.788 eV), with Fukui electrophilicity localized on O1, O3, and O4. MD simulations on Fe(110) indicate spontaneous, stable adsorption, supporting the proposed mechanism.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Background – Stress in childhood and adolescence can disrupt emotional, cognitive, and physiological development and contribute to long-term health consequences. Conventional assessments, such as cortisol sampling and retrospective questionnaires, are often invasive, burdensome, and poorly suited for repeated pediatric use. Advances in mobile health, wearable devices, and other non-invasive sensing approaches offer new opportunities for real-time stress detection, monitoring, and mitigation in children and adolescents. Objective – This scoping review synthesizes evidence on non-invasive technologies for pediatric stress detection, monitoring, and mitigation, with attention to mobile, wearable, and ubiquitous health applications. It maps reported technologies, protocols, study contexts, and intervention approaches, and identifies gaps for future research and practice. Methods – Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, four bibliographic databases–PubMed, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and ACM Digital Library–were searched, with Google Scholar screened as a supplementary source. Searches covered peer-reviewed studies published from January 2013 to April 2026. Eligible studies involved participants aged 0–18 years, evaluated non-invasive technological methods for stress detection, monitoring, or mitigation, and reported empirical outcomes. Data were charted across technology type, stress induction and validation, study context, age group, evaluation method, datasets, and intervention strategies. Results – Thirty-four studies were included. Wearable and mobile sensing approaches dominated the literature, while fewer studies examined non-contact, ambient, or hybrid systems. Stress induction and assessment methods were heterogeneous, often relying on task-based, situational, or context-specific stressors rather than standardized pediatric protocols. Studies were conducted in school, laboratory, home, therapy, and emerging clinical contexts, although longitudinal real-world deployments remained limited. Children under 13 years were more frequently represented than adolescents, while younger children and developmentally diverse populations remained unevenly studied. A smaller subset examined mitigation strategies, including biofeedback, serious games, smart objects, and caregiver- or parent-mediated interventions. Ethical, privacy, and implementation issues were acknowledged but not systematically addressed. Conclusions – Non-invasive technologies show strong potential for pediatric stress detection, monitoring, and mitigation, particularly through wearable, mobile, and interactive systems. However, the field remains methodologically fragmented. Future work should develop age-appropriate stress protocols, improve dataset diversity and transparency, conduct ecologically valid longitudinal evaluations, and strengthen ethical, privacy, and equity considerations for translation into schools, homes, telehealth, and clinical care.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: We develop a conservative finite-volume Buckley–Leverett solver equipped with a bounded-interval multiwavelet state-analysis layer. Because non-capillary Buckley–Leverett transport is a nonlinear hyperbolic conservation law with entropy-admissible shocks, the saturation equation is advanced by a conservative finite-volume method with monotone numerical fluxes. The accepted finite-volume state is then embedded in a bounded-domain multiwavelet hierarchy, reconstructed back to cell averages, and used for multiresolution diagnostics. The formal transport accuracy is therefore governed by the underlying finite-volume discretization, while the multiwavelet layer is used for representation, compression, and front-localization diagnostics. Its purpose is instead to quantify whether the deterministic physical-space saturation state can be represented faithfully, compressed in a controlled manner, and used to identify dynamically active front regions. Validation against reference Buckley–Leverett profiles for a Berea benchmark shows accurate saturation histories, spatial profiles, front-position diagnostics, and mass balance. The multiwavelet reconstruction tracks the internal finite-volume state with essentially exact fidelity. Additional thresholding tests show that a substantial fraction of detail coefficients can be discarded while maintaining small reconstruction errors and negligible global mass defect, and fine-level detail activity localizes the moving displacement front. The resulting formulation provides a conservative and reproducible first stage toward future transport-active adaptive multiwavelet solvers for porous-media flow.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Magnetic particles (MPs) and quantum dots (QDs) are highly attractive for biomedical imaging, yet their broader application is often limited by poor aqueous dispersibility and instability. mods:mods.mods:abstract: This paper presents SPINDER, a compact 18-DoF hexapod robot designed for reproducible bio-inspired locomotion research. The platform integrates a time-of-flight depth camera, six-axis inertial measurement unit, and per-foot contact switches, with computation split between an ARM-based single-board computer and a real-time microcontroller driving Dynamixel actuators. We derive a closed-form inverse kinematics solver for the yaw-pitch-pitch leg configuration that enforces workspace feasibility and handles kinematic singularities, achieving real time computations per leg. The locomotion controller combines a coupled-oscillator central pattern generator for inter-leg coordination with local motion controllers that regulate torso motion and generate cycloid-based swing trajectories with stance compensation, before mapping foot targets to joint commands via analytic IK. Hardware experiments demonstrate stable tripod, ripple, and wave locomotion, including omnidirectional commands, smooth online gait transitions that settle within approximately two gait cycles, and successful traversal of structured uneven terrain (height variations up to 18 mm) with 100% completion rate and mean body-pitch deviation below 5. All mechanical designs, kinematic models, and control software will be released to support replication and extension.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Groundwater quality assessment in arid regions requires methods that are accurate, transparent, and useful for drinking-water and irrigation management. This study presents an integrated hydrochemical and interpretable machine-learning assessment of groundwater quality in Al-Jouf, Saudi Arabia, using descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, principal component analysis (PCA), water quality index (WQI), irrigation indices, and comparative artificial intelligence modelling. Because WQI is deterministically calculated from physicochemical parameters, machine learning was used not to replace the WQI equation, but to provide an interpretable screening framework for identifying dominant hydrochemical drivers and supporting future reduced-parameter monitoring. Results showed strong interdependence among EC, TDS, Na+, Ca2+, Mg2+, and Cl−, while PCA identified mineralization as the main control on groundwater variability. WQI ranged from 27.3 to 865.3, with more than two-thirds of samples classified as poor to unfit for drinking. Irrigation assessment, based on EC salinity hazard, SAR, Na%, and Wilcox classification, indicated dominant high to very high salinity hazards (C3–C4); where indicators differed, the more restrictive class was prioritized for management. Among six benchmarked algorithms, the Explainable Boosting Machine (EBM) provided the best balance between predictive performance, stability, and interpretability. Feature-importance analysis identified salinity- and hardness-related variables as the main drivers of groundwater-quality deterioration. The findings show that EBM can support transparent groundwater screening, monitoring prioritization, and targeted treatment or irrigation-control decisions in arid aquifer systems.
